chunks: My father narrated to us, may God be pleased with him, saying: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated to us, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Khazzaz, from Al-Fadl al-Ash'ari, from Al-Husayn ibn al-Mukhtar, from Abi Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Job (peace be upon him) was tested for seven years without having committed any sin.
ai.seo_question: How long was Prophet Job tested and was it due to his sins?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that Prophet Job’s seven-year affliction was a divine trial (ibtala) rather than retribution for sin, a nuance emphasized in Shaykh al-Saduq’s *al-Khisal* to distinguish between testing and punishment. This tradition underscores the Shia theological view that the righteous may endure prolonged hardship as a means of spiritual elevation and purification, independent of their moral standing.
